market_pricing_in: At $23.46 per share, the market is pricing in the rapid obsolescence of Yelp's core local advertising marketplace, treating the business as a melting ice cube burdened by search engine disintermediation and merchant pricing exhaustion. Despite a low headline GAAP P/E (~11x), the stock trades at an audited Owner Earnings multiple (P/OE) of 46.1x and EV/OE of 46.3x (Owner Yield of 2.2%), reflecting how heavily stock-based compensation ($100.6 million) dilutes true cash flow generation. Mr. Market views Yelp as an endangered top-of-funnel bridge asset being disintermediated by zero-click AI search results. Google AI Overviews now populate approximately 68% of local business queries, generating synthesized reviews directly on search engine results pages and driving a reported 58% drop in top-position organic click-through rates to Yelp. This structural decay in user discovery has caused organic ad click volumes to contract for three consecutive quarters (-11% in Q3 2025, -7% in Q4 2025, and -5% YoY in Q2 2026). Concurrently, Yelp's primary pricing lever—raising Cost-Per-Click (CPC) rates to offset traffic drops—has reached total exhaustion, slowing from +14% growth in early 2025 to just +1% YoY in Q2 2026 as small business advertisers resist further price increases. Paying ad locations dropped to 510,000 (-1% YoY), while six-month accounts receivable credit loss provisions surged to $18.0 million. To fund defensive M&A (the $271.2 million cash purchase of Hatch), management drew down $100 million on its credit facility, leaving net debt at $-0.11 per share ($-6 million net cash/debt position) and forcing a complete pause on share repurchases, removing the primary financial engineering bid supporting EPS.
why_it_might_be_right:
The market's punitive valuation is mathematically grounded when evaluating Yelp on true Owner Earnings rather than unadjusted GAAP net income or Adjusted EBITDA. The transition from GAAP metrics to unencumbered cash generation reveals severe structural fragility under an accelerated decay scenario:

1. Starting True Owner Earnings: $0.51 per share ($28.3 million total, calculated after deducting $100.6 million in annual stock-based compensation and $33.4 million in maintenance CapEx from operating cash flow).
2. Skeptic Exit Multiple: 10.0x P/OE, a compressed valuation appropriate for a secularly declining digital ad marketplace plagued by persistent dilution.
3. Terminal Operating Value at Stagnation: If ad click drops (-5%) and merchant churn force true Owner Earnings to remain flat at $0.51 per share over a 5-year horizon, a 10.0x multiple yields an operating business value of $5.10 per share.
4. Net Debt Adjustment: Subtracting $-0.11 per share in net balance sheet debt ($6 million net debt following the Hatch acquisition) yields an implied 5-year target price of $4.99 per share.
5. Implied Annualized Return: Declining from today's $23.46 market price to $4.99 over 5 years results in an annualized return of -26.7% CAGR.
6. Fundamental Grounding: This downside scenario is fully supported by operational realities: 3,400 out of Yelp's 5,100 employees work in an aggressive outbound sales force facing rising Customer Acquisition Costs (CAC), while Google AI Overviews systematically sever external organic traffic flows to Yelp's platform.
how_things_are_going_now: Yelp's operating performance reflects a stark operational divergence between its decaying legacy ad engine and its emerging non-ad monetization channels. In Q2 2026, total net revenue reached $375.5–$376.0 million (+1.0% to +1.4% YoY), marking a sharp deceleration from historical mid-single-digit growth, while Q4 2025 previously registered the platform's first top-line YoY contraction (-0.54%) in four years. Full-year 2026 guidance was narrowed to $1.460–$1.470 billion (~0%–1% YoY growth). Core advertising revenue contracted -3% YoY to $342.5 million, severely dragged down by the Restaurants, Retail & Other (RR&O) division, which fell -10% YoY to $101.5 million due to merchant churn and ad click declines. The core Services segment ($241.0 million) remained flat YoY as high interest rates suppressed discretionary home remodeling projects, though non-discretionary repair categories (HVAC, plumbing) maintained baseline stability. Conversely, non-advertising 'Other Revenue' (SaaS, Yelp Places API, and data licensing) surged +98% YoY to $33.0 million, supported by data licensing agreements and the integration of Hatch ($271.2 million acquisition contributing ~$35 million in ARR). Overall profitability is under visible pressure: Q2 GAAP Net Income fell 28% YoY to $31.7 million (margins contracting 300 bps to 8%), Adjusted EBITDA dropped 9% YoY to $91.0 million (24.2% margin), and Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is guided down sequentially to $70–$75 million. Audited Owner ROIC remains depressed at 4.3% due to high SBC and acquisition capital intensity.
what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
If Yelp's core Services ad engine stabilizes while its high-margin software acquisitions and API data licensing efforts continue to compound toward management's target of $250 million in Other Revenue ARR by 2028, true Owner Earnings can experience modest expansion. Below is a grounded continuation scenario over a 5-year investment horizon:

1. Starting True Owner Earnings: $0.51 per share ($28.3 million total).
2. Conservative Compounding Rate: Assuming Owner Earnings grow at a modest 4.0% CAGR as +98% growth in Other Revenue offsets core ad volume decay, Year 5 Owner Earnings reach $0.62 per share ($0.51 * 1.04^5 = $0.6205).
3. Prudent Terminal Multiple: Applying a 12.0x P/OE multiple—commensurate with a narrow-moat, low-growth digital media asset with high share dilution—yields an operating business value of $7.44 per share ($0.6205 * 12.0 = $7.446).
4. Balance Sheet Adjustment: Subtracting $-0.11 per share in net debt results in an expected Year 5 target share price of $7.33 per share ($7.446 - $0.11 = $7.336).
5. Implied 5-Year Annualized Return: From today's entry price of $23.46, a $7.33 terminal price yields an annualized return (IRR) of -20.8% per year.

Conclusion: Because Yelp heavily dilutes shareholders with $100.6 million in annual stock-based compensation, its true cash Owner Earnings ($0.51/share) represent a 46.1x P/OE multiple despite an unadjusted 11x GAAP P/E. Without structural cuts to share issuances and outbound sales force overhead, Yelp offers no margin of safety at $23.46.
full_html_content:
What the Market is Pricing In

At $23.46 per share, the market is pricing in the rapid obsolescence of Yelp's core local advertising marketplace, treating the business as a melting ice cube burdened by search engine disintermediation and merchant pricing exhaustion. Despite a low headline GAAP P/E (~11x), the stock trades at an audited Owner Earnings multiple (P/OE) of 46.1x and EV/OE of 46.3x (Owner Yield of 2.2%), reflecting how heavily stock-based compensation ($100.6 million) dilutes true cash flow generation. Mr. Market views Yelp as an endangered top-of-funnel bridge asset being disintermediated by zero-click AI search results. Google AI Overviews now populate approximately 68% of local business queries, generating synthesized reviews directly on search engine results pages and driving a reported 58% drop in top-position organic click-through rates to Yelp. This structural decay in user discovery has caused organic ad click volumes to contract for three consecutive quarters (-11% in Q3 2025, -7% in Q4 2025, and -5% YoY in Q2 2026). Concurrently, Yelp's primary pricing lever—raising Cost-Per-Click (CPC) rates to offset traffic drops—has reached total exhaustion, slowing from +14% growth in early 2025 to just +1% YoY in Q2 2026 as small business advertisers resist further price increases. Paying ad locations dropped to 510,000 (-1% YoY), while six-month accounts receivable credit loss provisions surged to $18.0 million. To fund defensive M&A (the $271.2 million cash purchase of Hatch), management drew down $100 million on its credit facility, leaving net debt at \(-0.11 per share (\)-6 million net cash/debt position) and forcing a complete pause on share repurchases, removing the primary financial engineering bid supporting EPS.

Why the Market Might Be Right

The market's punitive valuation is mathematically grounded when evaluating Yelp on true Owner Earnings rather than unadjusted GAAP net income or Adjusted EBITDA. The transition from GAAP metrics to unencumbered cash generation reveals severe structural fragility under an accelerated decay scenario:

1
Starting True Owner Earnings
$0.51 per share ($28.3 million total, calculated after deducting $100.6 million in annual stock-based compensation and $33.4 million in maintenance CapEx from operating cash flow).
2

10.0x P/OE, a compressed valuation appropriate for a secularly declining digital ad marketplace plagued by persistent dilution.
3
Terminal Operating Value at Stagnation
If ad click drops (-5%) and merchant churn force true Owner Earnings to remain flat at $0.51 per share over a 5-year horizon, a 10.0x multiple yields an operating business value of $5.10 per share.
4

Subtracting $-0.11 per share in net balance sheet debt ($6 million net debt following the Hatch acquisition) yields an implied 5-year target price of $4.99 per share.
5

Declining from today's $23.46 market price to $4.99 over 5 years results in an annualized return of -26.7% CAGR.
6
Fundamental Grounding
This downside scenario is fully supported by operational realities: 3,400 out of Yelp's 5,100 employees work in an aggressive outbound sales force facing rising Customer Acquisition Costs (CAC), while Google AI Overviews systematically sever external organic traffic flows to Yelp's platform.

How Things Are Going Now

Yelp's operating performance reflects a stark operational divergence between its decaying legacy ad engine and its emerging non-ad monetization channels. In Q2 2026, total net revenue reached $375.5–$376.0 million (+1.0% to +1.4% YoY), marking a sharp deceleration from historical mid-single-digit growth, while Q4 2025 previously registered the platform's first top-line YoY contraction (-0.54%) in four years. Full-year 2026 guidance was narrowed to $1.460–$1.470 billion (~0%–1% YoY growth). Core advertising revenue contracted -3% YoY to $342.5 million, severely dragged down by the Restaurants, Retail & Other (RR&O) division, which fell -10% YoY to $101.5 million due to merchant churn and ad click declines. The core Services segment ($241.0 million) remained flat YoY as high interest rates suppressed discretionary home remodeling projects, though non-discretionary repair categories (HVAC, plumbing) maintained baseline stability. Conversely, non-advertising 'Other Revenue' (SaaS, Yelp Places API, and data licensing) surged +98% YoY to $33.0 million, supported by data licensing agreements and the integration of Hatch ($271.2 million acquisition contributing ~$35 million in ARR). Overall profitability is under visible pressure: Q2 GAAP Net Income fell 28% YoY to $31.7 million (margins contracting 300 bps to 8%), Adjusted EBITDA dropped 9% YoY to $91.0 million (24.2% margin), and Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is guided down sequentially to $70–$75 million. Audited Owner ROIC remains depressed at 4.3% due to high SBC and acquisition capital intensity.

What If It Keeps Going That Way

If Yelp's core Services ad engine stabilizes while its high-margin software acquisitions and API data licensing efforts continue to compound toward management's target of $250 million in Other Revenue ARR by 2028, true Owner Earnings can experience modest expansion. Below is a grounded continuation scenario over a 5-year investment horizon:

1
Starting True Owner Earnings
$0.51 per share ($28.3 million total).
2
Conservative Compounding Rate
Assuming Owner Earnings grow at a modest 4.0% CAGR as +98% growth in Other Revenue offsets core ad volume decay, Year 5 Owner Earnings reach $0.62 per share ($0.51 1.04^5 = $0.6205).
3
Prudent Terminal Multiple
Applying a 12.0x P/OE multiple—commensurate with a narrow-moat, low-growth digital media asset with high share dilution—yields an operating business value of $7.44 per share ($0.6205 12.0 = $7.446).
4
Balance Sheet Adjustment
Subtracting $-0.11 per share in net debt results in an expected Year 5 target share price of $7.33 per share ($7.446 - $0.11 = $7.336).
5
Implied 5-Year Annualized Return
From today's entry price of $23.46, a $7.33 terminal price yields an annualized return (IRR) of -20.8% per year.

Conclusion: Because Yelp heavily dilutes shareholders with $100.6 million in annual stock-based compensation, its true cash Owner Earnings ($0.51/share) represent a 46.1x P/OE multiple despite an unadjusted 11x GAAP P/E. Without structural cuts to share issuances and outbound sales force overhead, Yelp offers no margin of safety at $23.46.
